title: Dimension of a finite normalization of a universally catenary local domain
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian universally catenary local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, and let $C'$ be the integral closure of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], finite as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A local ring has one maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero with no zero divisors. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C'$ whose contraction to $C$ is the maximal ideal of $C$, one has $\dim(C'_{\mathfrak m})=\dim C$, where localization is as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.document: literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex; Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Tag 02IJ (lemma-dimension-formula), equality for a universally catenary base, specialized to the finite birational domain extension C ⊂ C′. This is the normalization dimension input cited as [8, Theorem 5.6.10] in Greco Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9).

proof.text: Set C′ = integralClosure C K and p = maximalIdeal C. The map C → C′ is injective because its composite with C′ → K is the injective fraction-ring map. Module finiteness makes C′ a finite-type integral C-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], hence algebraic, so trdeg_C C′ = 0 [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Equip κ(m) with the κ(p)-algebra structure from Ideal.ResidueField.map and hm.symm. Its compatibility with the original algebra maps gives the scalar tower C → κ(p) → κ(m). Since m is maximal, κ(m) is finite over C′, hence finite and integral over C. Integrality ascends the scalar tower, so κ(m) is integral and algebraic over κ(p), and its transcendence degree is zero. This uses Mathlib Module.Finite.trans, Algebra.IsIntegral.tower_top, Algebra.IsIntegral.isAlgebraic and trdeg_eq_zero.

source.place: Tag 02IJ specialization: finite integral birational extension has zero fraction-field and residue-field transcendence degrees.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain] to $R=C$, $S=C′$, $\mathfrak p$ the maximal ideal of $C$, and the given maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $C′$. Its hypotheses hold by the assumptions and Step 1, and Step 1 makes both transcendence-degree terms zero. Hence $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak m)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (lemma-dimension-formula), equality clause for a universally catenary base; specialize to the finite normalization.

proof.text: Use IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] to identify dim(C′_m) with height(m). Mathlib IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_height_eq_ringKrullDim identifies height(p) with dim C. Rewrite by the height equality of Step 2. No chain construction or positive-dimension hypothesis is necessary.
